title: docs: add RAG templates, agents/tool-calling quickstarts, and docs site examples
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Add first-class RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) templates plus two new agent/tool-calling quickstarts and corresponding docs site examples. Motivation: customers frequently ask for end-to-end examples that combine embeddings, vector stores, and agent-style tool calls (search, db lookup, external API). This PR bundles reusable templates and copy-first quickstarts so devs can boot a RAG flow in minutes and see recommended prompt structure, caching guidance, and error-handling patterns.

What this PR includes: 1) /docs/guides/rag.md - a canonical RAG guide with architecture diagram, when-to-use rules, and recommended model/quantization profiles; 2) /examples/rag-templates/ - three templates (simple-read, conversational-rag, batch-indexing) with sample prompts and test vectors; 3) /examples/agents/tool-calling/ - two agent samples: a web-scrape + search agent and a db-lookup + tool-fallback agent demonstrating function/tool calling patterns and structured output; 4) updates to the docs site navigation and quickstart landing page so examples are discoverable; 5) a playground preview link for interactive examples.

Checklist: * [x] guide + templates written and unit-tested where applicable * [x] docs site integration + markdown frontmatter * [x] example code uses existing SDKs (python/typescript) and references redwood SDK patterns * [x] link-check and spellcheck passed * [x] reviewers addressed feedback on prompt framing and security notes

Notes for reviewers: focus on clarity of the RAG decision flow, whether the agent examples demonstrate safe fallback behavior, and whether the quickstart will run for users with free-tier credentials (we default to a small example dataset and ephemeral vector store). Related: ENG-1029 (RAG template standardization), PM-374 (quickstarts prioritization).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial rag guide and template scaffolding; add simple-read and conversational examples; add agent tool-calling samples (python + ts); docs site nav and frontmatter updates; polish prompt wording and add test vectors
review_comments: Miguel Hernandez: Please add a short security section about allowing external tool calls; recommend defaulting to a sandboxed scraping tool.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Good catch — added security notes to rag.md and switched example scraper to the sandboxed client. Also added a note about rate limits.
Sophie Lin: The conversational-rag prompt looks likely to hallucinate on missing context; add a strict 'no-hallucination' guard and fallback to 'I don't know' — also add a unit test.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Added 'no-hallucination' guard and test vector; updated example.py to return structured fallback when evidence score < threshold.
Ethan Zhao: Minor: site navigation order should place Quickstarts above Tutorials. Also run link-check CI.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Reordered quickstarts in site config and fixed two broken links found by link-check. CI green now.
Miguel Hernandez: Approved after security notes and tests were added.
release_notes:

- Added two agent/tool-calling examples demonstrating web-scrape and db-fallback patterns

notes_for_backport: No backport required; docs-only change. If requested, cherry-pick to release/2026-Q1 to keep docs branch in sync.
testing_instructions: 1) Follow examples/rag-templates/README.md to run the simple-read example (small csv included). 2) For agents, see README in each agent folder; use sandboxed tool clients by default. 3) Run ./scripts/ci/check-links.sh and pytest tests/examples to validate examples.
